question:
Statements: All teachers are graduates. Some graduates work in schools.
Conclusion I: Some teachers work in schools.
Conclusion II: Some school workers are graduates.
Which conclusions follow?
explanation: I does not follow — the graduates who work in schools may not be teachers. II follows directly from 'some graduates work in schools' by simple conversion (some school workers are graduates).

question:
Statements: All cats are animals. All animals breathe.
Conclusion I: All cats breathe.
Conclusion II: Some animals are cats.
Which conclusions follow?
explanation: I: All cats→animals, all animals breathe → all cats breathe (valid chain). II: 'All cats are animals' converts to 'some animals are cats' (valid partial conversion). Both follow.

question:
Statements: No student is a teacher. All teachers hold degrees. Some degree holders are professors.
Conclusion I: No student holds a degree.
Conclusion II: Some degree holders are teachers.
Which conclusions necessarily follow?
explanation: I does not follow — students may independently hold degrees even though no student is a teacher. II follows by converting 'All teachers hold degrees' → 'Some degree holders are teachers'.

question:
Statements: All politicians are liars. Some liars are criminals.
Conclusion I: Some politicians are criminals.
Conclusion II: Some criminals are liars.
Conclusion III: All criminals are politicians.
Which conclusions follow?
explanation: I: Cannot conclude — criminal liars may not be politicians. II: Converts 'some liars are criminals' → 'some criminals are liars' ✓. III: Clearly false — criminals being liars doesn't make them politicians.

question: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was cancelled. What can we conclude?

options.B: It may or may not have rained

explanation: Affirming the consequent is a fallacy. The match could have been cancelled for many reasons. We cannot conclude it rained.

question: If a student studies hard, they pass. Ali did not pass. What can we conclude?
explanation: Modus Tollens: P→Q and ¬Q implies ¬P. Ali did not pass (¬Q), therefore Ali did not study hard (¬P).

question: 'All on-time employees receive a bonus. All bonus recipients are happy.' Sara is not happy. Which must be true?

options.C: Sara received a bonus but is unhappy
options.D: Sara was on time but received no bonus

explanation: Apply contrapositive twice: Sara not happy → Sara got no bonus → Sara was not on time.

question: Given: If X then Y. If Y then Z. If not-Z then W. W is false. Which statement must be true?
explanation: W is false (¬W). The contrapositive of 'If ¬Z then W' is '¬W → Z'. Therefore Z must be true. We cannot determine X or Y from this information alone.

question: Claim: 'Drinking coffee improves concentration.' Which of the following most strengthens this claim?

options.A: A controlled study showed coffee drinkers scored 30% higher on standardised focus tests
options.B: Some coffee drinkers still have poor concentration
options.D: Coffee is sold in shops worldwide

explanation: A provides direct empirical evidence with a measurable effect from a controlled study — the strongest form of support.

question: Argument: 'Electric car sales rose 40% last year because fuel prices increased.' Which most weakens this?

options.A: Electric cars are quieter than petrol cars
options.B: Most electric car purchases were contracted before fuel prices rose

explanation: B breaks the causal link by showing the purchases were decided before the alleged cause (fuel price rise) took effect.

question: Argument: 'Students who read novels score higher on language tests; therefore schools should mandate novel reading.' Which best strengthens this?

options.A: Novels must be purchased, adding cost to schools
options.B: Higher language test scores predict better long-term career outcomes
options.C: Novel readers showed no advantage in mathematics
options.D: Schools already assign some novels as homework

explanation: B links the intermediate benefit (higher language scores) to a valued real-world outcome (career success), making the policy recommendation well-justified.

question: Argument: 'Area X has more trees than Area Y, and Area X has lower crime rates. Therefore trees reduce crime.' Which most weakens this?

options.A: Trees provide shade and lower ambient temperature
options.B: Area X also has significantly higher average income than Area Y
options.C: Some high-tree neighbourhoods report high crime

explanation: B introduces a confounding variable (income) that could independently explain both more trees (wealthier areas invest in parks) and lower crime. This is a classic alternative-cause weakener.

question: 'We should hire Asim because he has five years of experience.' The underlying assumption is:

options.B: Experience is relevant to this job's performance
options.C: Five years is unusually long in this industry
options.D: Asim has no competitors for this role

explanation: Without assuming that experience is predictive of job performance, citing years of experience gives no rational basis for the hiring recommendation.

question: 'This drug cures Disease X in lab mice, so it should be approved for human use.' The argument assumes:

options.A: The drug was expensive to develop
options.B: Results in mice reliably transfer to human physiology
options.C: Disease X is extremely common in humans
options.D: Lab mice are inexpensive to maintain

explanation: The argument bridges animal results to human approval. This only makes sense if mouse outcomes predict human outcomes — an assumption that must hold for the conclusion to follow.

question: 'Raising the minimum wage will help low-income workers.' A critical unstated assumption is:

options.A: All workers currently earn minimum wage
options.B: Employers will not reduce hours or lay off workers in response
options.C: The minimum wage is currently extremely low

explanation: If employers offset the wage increase by cutting hours or jobs, raising the minimum wage could harm rather than help low-income workers. The conclusion requires this not to happen.

question: 'This bridge was built 50 years ago and is still standing, so it is safe.' The conclusion relies on assuming:

options.A: The bridge has never undergone repairs
options.C: Longevity alone is sufficient evidence of current structural safety
options.D: Engineers designed it to last a century

explanation: The argument conflates historical endurance with present-day safety — an assumption that must hold for the conclusion 'it is safe' to follow from 'it is still standing'.

question: Despite a record harvest this year, many farmers are in severe financial distress. Which best explains this paradox?

options.B: The bumper crop flooded the market, crashing commodity prices below production costs
options.D: The government raised agricultural taxes this year

explanation: When supply dramatically exceeds demand, prices collapse. A record harvest can paradoxically destroy farm income by driving revenue below the cost of producing the crop.

question: Citizens of Country A consume more calories per day on average than those of Country B, yet Country A has a lower obesity rate. Which best resolves this?

options.A: Country A has a higher GDP
options.B: Country A has better hospitals and healthcare
options.C: People in Country A have significantly more physically active lifestyles and higher average metabolic rates
options.D: Country B enforces stricter food-labelling laws

explanation: Higher calorie intake paired with lower obesity is explained by higher caloric expenditure. Greater physical activity means calories are burned rather than stored as fat.

question: A new highway was built specifically to reduce traffic congestion, yet congestion increased significantly after its completion. Which best explains this?

options.A: The highway carries high toll fees
options.B: The new road capacity attracted drivers who previously avoided that route, generating induced demand
options.C: The speed limit on the highway is too low
options.D: The highway passes through a sparsely populated area

explanation: This is the induced demand phenomenon: new road capacity attracts new traffic, often negating or reversing the intended congestion relief.

question: A school launched a tutoring programme to help failing students. Yet the school's overall average test score dropped after the programme began. Which best explains this?

options.A: Tutoring is generally ineffective for all students
options.B: The programme's reputation attracted many new enrolees with learning difficulties; even as individual scores improved, a larger proportion of low scorers lowered the aggregate average
options.C: Teachers reduced their effort after the programme started
options.D: The tests were made harder that same year

explanation: The paradox is resolved by a change in population composition: more low-scoring students enrolled. Even if each student's score improved, a larger share of low scorers can pull the overall average down.

question: A company's revenue was Rs. 500,000 in 2022 and Rs. 600,000 in 2023. By what percentage did revenue increase?
A budget of Rs. 400,000 is split: Department A gets 25%, B gets 35%, C gets 30%, and D gets the remainder. How much does Department D receive?
explanation: A + B + C = 90%. Department D receives 10% of Rs. 400,000 = Rs. 40,000.

question: Five students scored: Ali 72, Sara 85, Hina 60, Zaid 90, Raza 78. What is their mean score?
Monthly sales (in thousands of Rs.): Jan 40, Feb 50, Mar 35, Apr 60, May 55. What is the average monthly sale over this five-month period?
A factory's quarterly output: Q1 = 1,200 units, Q2 = 1,500, Q3 = 1,350, Q4 = 1,650. The quarterly target was 1,400 units. In how many quarters did the factory meet or exceed its target?
Four people A, B, C, D sit in a row. A is at the leftmost seat. D is at the rightmost seat. B is to the left of C. What is the order from left to right?
explanation: A = position 1, D = position 4. B is left of C, so middle positions must be B then C: order is A, B, C, D.

question: Six students sit in a row. Zaid is at position 3. Sara is immediately to Zaid's right. Ali is at the leftmost position. Which statement must be true?
explanation: Zaid is at position 3. Immediately to his right = position 4. Therefore Sara is at position 4.

question: Five books — History (H), Math (M), Science (S), English (E), Art (A) — are on a shelf. H is between M and S. E is to the right of S. A is at the leftmost position. What is the correct left-to-right order?
explanation: A = 1st. H is between M and S with E to S's right. Placing: A(1), M(2), H(3), S(4), E(5) satisfies all conditions: H between M and S ✓, E right of S ✓.

question: In a row of 8 students, Ayesha is 3rd from the left and Bilal is 5th from the right. How many students sit between them?
explanation: Bilal's position from left = 8 − 5 + 1 = 4th. Ayesha is 3rd. They occupy adjacent positions 3 and 4, so 0 students sit between them.

question: Five executives P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row. P is not at either end. Q is at position 2. R is immediately to Q's right. S is at the rightmost position. T is not adjacent to P. At which position does P sit?
explanation: Q=2, R=3 (right of Q), S=5. P cannot be at ends (not 1 or 5) and position 3 is taken by R, so P = 4. T fills position 1. T(1) and P(4) are not adjacent ✓.

question: Six people A, B, C, D, E, F sit in a circle. A is directly opposite D. B is directly opposite E. C is directly opposite F. B is immediately to A's right (clockwise). Who is immediately to D's left (counterclockwise)?
explanation: Clockwise: A(1), B(2), C(3), D(4), E(5), F(6). Immediately to D's left (counterclockwise from D) = position 3 = C.

question: Five people P, Q, R, S, T sit around a circular table. P is immediately to Q's left. R is immediately to Q's right. S is not adjacent to P. T is between S and P (adjacent to both). What is the clockwise order starting from P?
explanation: Clockwise: P(1), Q(2), R(3). Remaining: S and T at 4 and 5. S not adjacent to P means S ≠ 5 (position 5 is adjacent to P at 1). So S=4, T=5. T(5) is between S(4) and P(1) ✓. Order: P, Q, R, S, T.

question: Six people A, B, C, D, E, F sit around a circular table. A and D are directly opposite each other. B is immediately to A's right. C is immediately to D's right. F is not adjacent to A. Who sits immediately to C's right?
explanation: Clockwise: A(1), B(2), ?(3), D(4), C(5), ?(6). F cannot be adjacent to A, so F ≠ 6 (adjacent to A) and F ≠ 2 (= B). F = 3, E = 6. Immediately to C's (position 5) right = position 6 = E.

question: Six people P, Q, R, S, T, U sit around a circular table. P is directly opposite S. Q is 2 seats clockwise from P. T is directly opposite Q. R is adjacent to both T and S (sitting between them clockwise). What is U's position relative to P?
explanation: P=1, S=4 (opposite), Q=3 (2 clockwise from P), T=6 (opposite Q), R=5 (between T and S clockwise, adjacent to both). Remaining seat: position 2 = U. Position 2 is immediately to P's (1) right. ✓

question: Pointing to a photo, Zara says, 'This man is the father of my son.' How is the man in the photo related to Zara?
explanation: The father of Zara's son is Zara's husband.

question: A is B's mother and B is C's sister. How is A related to C?
explanation: B is C's sister, and A is B's mother; therefore A is also C's mother.

question: Introducing a man to her friend, Hina says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to Hina?
explanation: The only daughter of Hina's father is Hina herself. So the man's mother = Hina, making the man Hina's son.

question: Pointing to a man in a photo, Dania says: 'The sister of this man's father is my mother.' How is Dania related to the man?
explanation: The man's father's sister = Dania's mother. So the man's father and Dania's mother are siblings. The man's father is Dania's uncle; the man (son of Dania's uncle) is Dania's cousin.

question: Tariq walks 5 km North, then turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. In which direction is he now facing?
explanation: Start facing North → turn right = East → turn right = South. He is now facing South.

question: Sana faces North. She turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anti-clockwise. Which direction does she face now?
explanation: North → 90° clockwise = East → 180° anti-clockwise = East − 180° = West.

question: Starting from point A, Kamran walks 8 km East to B, then 6 km North to C. What is the shortest distance from A to C?
explanation: By Pythagoras: AC = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 km.

question: Aman starts at X. He walks 10 km North to Y, turns left and walks 5 km to Z, turns left and walks 10 km to W, then turns right and walks 3 km to V. What is the straight-line distance from X to V?
explanation: Using coordinates: X(0,0)→Y(0,10); turn left (West)→Z(−5,10); turn left (South)→W(−5,0); turn right (West)→V(−8,0). Distance XV = |−8 − 0| = 8 km (same y-coordinate).

question: If BOOK is coded as CPPL, what is the code for DOOR?
explanation: Each letter shifts +1: D→E, O→P, O→P, R→S. Code = EPPS.

question: In a code, MANGO is written as OCPIQ. What is APPLE coded as?
explanation: Each letter shifts +2: A→C, P→R, P→R, L→N, E→G. Code = CRRNG.

question: In a code: 'sun is bright' = 'ka na pa'; 'bright day ahead' = 'pa da sa'; 'is day clear' = 'na da ra'. What is the code for 'sun'?
explanation: 'bright' = pa (sentences 1 & 2); 'is' = na (sentences 1 & 3); 'day' = da (sentences 2 & 3). In sentence 1 — ka na pa — na = is, pa = bright, so ka = sun.

question: In a code, consonants are shifted +2 positions in the alphabet and vowels are shifted −1 (with wraparound: A→Z). What is VITAL coded as?
explanation: V(consonant)→X (+2); I(vowel)→H (−1); T(consonant)→V (+2); A(vowel)→Z (−1, wraparound A→Z); L(consonant)→N (+2). Code = XHVZN.

question: In a class of 30 students, Omer ranks 10th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
explanation: Rank from bottom = Total − Rank from top + 1 = 30 − 10 + 1 = 21.

question: Raza is taller than Bilal but shorter than Sana. Arif is taller than Raza but shorter than Iman. Sana is shorter than Iman. Who is the tallest?
explanation: Chain: Bilal < Raza < Sana < Iman, and Raza < Arif < Iman. Iman is taller than everyone.

question: Asad is 7th from the left in a row. He and Khalid exchange positions; Asad is then 14th from the left. Khalid was originally 11th from the right. How many children are in the row?
explanation: After the swap, Asad is at Khalid's original position: 14th from left = 11th from right. Total = 14 + 11 − 1 = 24.

question: Six athletes P, Q, R, S, T, U finish a race. Clues: (1) T finishes 2nd; (2) U finishes immediately after T; (3) R finishes before U; (4) Q finishes last (6th); (5) S finishes 5th; (6) P finishes after T but before Q. What is the finishing order?

options.A: R, T, U, P, S, Q
options.B: T, R, U, P, S, Q
options.C: R, U, T, P, S, Q
options.D: P, T, U, R, S, Q

explanation: T=2nd, U=3rd (immediately after T). R before U(3rd) → R=1st. S=5th, Q=6th. Remaining position 4th = P (after T, before Q ✓). Order: R, T, U, P, S, Q.
